name: HackerNoon
guidance: three.ws has partnered with HackerNoon, an independent tech publication, as a media home for its updates, technical write-ups and announcements. Say that and nothing grander: it is a publishing partnership, not an endorsement, a sponsorship or an editorial seal. HackerNoon pulls the three.ws RSS feed into a drafts queue; items are reviewed and then published with canonical URLs back to three.ws, so never say a post is auto-published or guaranteed to run. Talk about what a builder gets: a public feed anyone can subscribe to, and tutorials, deep-dives and integration guides.

features.title: The RSS feed HackerNoon reads
features.summary: Every three.ws announcement is published as a plain RSS 2.0 feed at three.ws/rss/announcements.xml. HackerNoon pulls it into a drafts queue, where each item is reviewed and published with a canonical URL back to three.ws.

facts.says: three.ws has partnered with HackerNoon, making HackerNoon the canonical media home for three.ws updates, technical write-ups, and product announcements.

facts.says: HackerNoon pulls every new post automatically from the three.ws RSS feed at three.ws/rss/announcements.xml.

facts.says: Each item lands in the three.ws HackerNoon drafts queue, is reviewed, then published, with canonical URLs pointing back to three.ws so search attribution stays with the source.
The feed is a plain RSS 2.0 document with a channel element, open to anyone to read.
The curated feed source is a single JSON file, so the team controls exactly what HackerNoon and any RSS reader sees.
The partnership gives three.ws a direct publishing channel into the HackerNoon audience without relying on social-media algorithms.

features.title: The newsroom behind the feed
features.summary: The three.ws newsroom lists every announcement, each with its own permalink, and one click opens the same items as the RSS feed HackerNoon reads.

facts.says: Every three.ws announcement lives in the newsroom at three.ws/news, and each one has its own permalink.
The newsroom links straight to the RSS feed, and the feed is a standard RSS 2.0 channel.
The same items the newsroom shows are the ones HackerNoon pulls from the feed.

features.title: A builder-focused publishing partnership
features.summary: three.ws and HackerNoon are launching a builder-focused initiative of feature articles, tutorials and developer guides for people shipping with AI, with a three.ws author page on HackerNoon.

steps.caption: three.ws has its own author page

facts.says: three.ws is partnering with HackerNoon to launch a builder-focused initiative with feature articles, tutorials, and developer guides for those shipping with AI.
The series covers feature-focused articles, hands-on tutorials, in-depth guides, and developer resources.
three.ws has its own author page on HackerNoon at hackernoon.com/u/three-ws.
The articles are written for builders actively shipping with AI, as well as enthusiasts following the space.
